children: ASML Holding NV Sponsored ADR (EURONEXT:ASML) rallied after reporting Q2 sales of $9.3B and raising 2026 sales guidance to $43–45B as CEO Christophe Fouquet warned U.S. export curbs could accelerate China’s domestic push while ASML expands High‑NA EUV ties with Samsung and repurchases stock.
: ASML (ASML) rallied across sessions. Q2 sales $9.3B, net income $2.9B. 2026 sales guide raised to $43–45B; gross margin 54–56%. Execution risk delivering EUV systems may affect bookings/shipments.
: ASML and Samsung agreed Sept. 8 to expand collaboration on High‑NA EUV and larger photomasks, aiming for High‑NA in high‑volume DRAM production by 2028 and co‑developing a 12‑inch mask platform.
: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet said U.S. export limits already block the company’s top EUV tools to China and warned wider curbs may speed China’s push for domestic chipmaking alternatives.
: ASML reported buyback transactions under its Jan 28, 2026 repurchase program in a MAR update; additional transaction details are available on the company website.
: JPMorgan and Wells Fargo kept overweight on ASML, raising targets to $2,400 and $2,500; RBC lifted its target to about $2,100, citing continued momentum and growth expectations for ASML.
: ASML (ASML) makes lithography equipment for advanced chips. CEO Christophe Fouquet said the AI-driven demand cycle may last 10–15 years, highlighting ASML’s role in chip production.
: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet was appointed nonexecutive director at Airbus, replacing Rene Obermann for the rest of his term; Fouquet will seek a full three-year mandate at the next AGM.
